45:1: Interpretation of Surah Al-Jathiya It is Meccan In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty guides His creation to reflect on His favors and blessings, and His great power by which He created the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of different creatures, races, and types of angels, jinn, humans, animals, birds, beasts, wild animals, and insects, and what is in the sea of diverse species and the alternation of night and day in their continuous, never-ending succession, this one with its darkness and that one with its light, and what God the Blessed and Exalted sends down of the clouds of rain at the time of need for it, and He called it provision because through it provision is obtained, And He revives thereby the earth after its death, that is, after it had been lifeless with no vegetation or anything in it. And His Almighty saying, And the directing of the winds, that is, south and north, south and south, land and sea, night and day. Some of it is for rain, some of it is for pollination, some of it is food for the souls, and some of it is sterile and does not produce. God Almighty said: First, Signs for the believers. Then they become certain, then they understand. This is a progression from a noble state to something more noble and higher. These verses are similar to the verse in Surat Al-Baqarah, which is the Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day and the [great] ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people and what God has sent down from the sky of water and revived thereby the earth after its lifelessness and dispersed therein every [kind of] moving creature and [His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who use reason.” Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih a long, strange hadith about the creation of man from the four humors, and God knows best.

45:6: God Almighty says: These are the verses of God, meaning the Qur’an, with its arguments and clear proofs. We recite them to you in truth, meaning they contain truth from truth. So if they do not believe in them and do not submit to them, then what message will they believe in after God and His verses? Then God the Almighty said: Woe to every slanderer and sinner. That is, a slanderer in his speech, a liar, a slanderer, a sinner in his actions, and whose heart is a disbeliever in the verses of God. For this reason, He said: He hears the verses of God recited to him, that is, they are read to him, then persists, that is, in his disbelief and denial out of arrogance and stubbornness, as if he had not heard them, that is, as if he had not heard them. Then give him tidings of a painful punishment, that is, inform him that he will have a painful and hurtful punishment with God the Almighty on the Day of Resurrection. And when he learns something of Our verses, he takes it in ridicule, that is, if he memorizes something from the Qur’an, he disbelieves in it and takes it in mockery and ridicule. For those is a humiliating punishment, that is, in return for belittling and mocking the Qur’an. For this reason, Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade traveling with the Qur’an to the land of the enemy for fear that the enemy would reach him. Then he explained the punishment that would befall him on the Day of Resurrection, saying: Behind them is Hell, that is, everyone who is characterized by that will become…” To Hell on the Day of Resurrection. And what they have earned will not avail them at all meaning, their wealth and children will not benefit them. And what they have taken as protectors other than God meaning, the gods they worshipped other than God will not avail them at all. And for them is a great punishment. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: This is guidance meaning the Qur’an. And those who disbelieve in the verses of their Lord will have a punishment of painful punishment meaning the painful, agonizing punishment. And God, the Exalted, the Majestic, knows best.

45:12: God the Almighty mentions His blessings upon His servants in what He has subjected to them of the sea that the ships may sail by His command. For He is the One who commanded the sea to carry them and that you may seek of His bounty that is, in trade and earnings and that you may be grateful that is, for obtaining the benefits brought from distant regions. Then the Almighty said: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth that is, of the planets, mountains, seas, and rivers, and everything that you benefit from, that is, all from His bounty, kindness, and grace. For this reason, He said: all from Him that is, from Him alone, with no partner in that, as the Almighty said: And whatever blessing you have is from God; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help. Ibn Jarir narrated, via Al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that God the Almighty said: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—all from Him everything is from God. That name contains one of His names, so all of that is from Him and no one disputes it, and it was confirmed that it is thus. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told us, al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Araka, who said: A man asked Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both: From what did He create creation? He said: From light, fire, darkness, and dust. He said: Go to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and ask him. So he went to him and said the same thing to him. Ibn Abbas said: Go back to Him and ask Him from what He created all of that. So he went back to him and asked him, and he recited: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. This is a strange narration and it contains something objectionable: Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. God the Almighty says: Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God. That is, to pardon them and endure the harm from them. This was at the beginning of Islam. They were commanded to be patient in the face of the harm caused by the polytheists and the People of the Book so that this would be a way to win them over. Then, when they persisted in their stubbornness, God prescribed fighting and jihad for the believers. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and Qatadah. Mujahid said: not expecting the days of God means they will not attain God's blessings. God the Almighty says: That He may reward a people for what they used to earn. That is, if you pardon them in this world, then God the Almighty will reward them for your bad deeds in the Hereafter. For this reason, God the Almighty says: "Whoever does righteousness does so for [his own] soul; and whoever does evil does so against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned." That is, you will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection and present your deeds to Him, and He will reward you for the good and the bad. And God the Almighty knows best.

45:21: God the Almighty says: The believers and the disbelievers are not equal, as He the Almighty said: "The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones." And God the Almighty said: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that is, they committed them and earned them that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds - equal in their life and their death? That is, that We will make them equal to them in this world and the hereafter. Evil is what they judge that is, evil is what they think of Us and Our justice that We will make the righteous and the wicked equal in the hereafter and in this world. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Mu'ammil ibn Ihab narrated to us, Bakir ibn Uthman al-Tanukhi narrated to us, al-Wadhin ibn Ata' narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Murthad al-Baji, on the authority of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him, who said: God the Almighty built His religion upon four pillars, so whoever is patient with them and does not act upon them will meet God among the wicked. It was said: What are they, O Abu Dharr? He said: What is lawful for God is for God, what is forbidden for God is for God, what God has commanded is for God, and what God has forbidden is for God. No one is to be trusted with them except God. Abu al-Qasim (peace be upon him) said: Just as grapes are not picked from thorns, so the wicked will not attain the dwellings of the righteous. This is a strange hadith from this aspect. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in his book, The Biography, that they found a stone in Mecca at the base of the Kaaba on which was written: You commit evil deeds and hope for good deeds, just as grapes are picked from thorns. At-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah from Abu al-Dhaha from Masruq that Tamim al-Dari stayed up all night until morning reciting this verse: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? For this reason God the Almighty said: Evil is that which they judge. And He the Almighty said: And God created the heavens and the earth in truth meaning with justice and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged. Then God the Almighty said: Have you seen he who has taken his own desire as his god? That is, he only follows his own desires, so whatever he deems good he does and whatever he deems bad he abandons. This may be used as evidence against the Mu'tazilah in their belief in rational goodness and badness. Malik, in what was narrated from him in the interpretation, said: No one desires anything except that he worships it. His statement, And God sent him astray, due to knowledge, has two possible interpretations: One is that God sent him astray because He knew that he deserved that, and the other is that God sent him astray after knowledge had reached him and proof had been established against him. The second entails the first and is not reversed. And He has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and over his vision a veil has been placed that is, so he does not hear what would benefit him, nor comprehend anything that would guide him, nor see any proof that would illuminate him. For this reason God the Almighty said: Then who can guide him after God? Then will you not be reminded? Like His statement, He whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide, and He leaves them wandering blindly in their transgression.

45:24: God Almighty tells us about the saying of the materialists among the infidels and those who agreed with them from the polytheists of the Arabs in denying the al-Qiyamah 75:“And they say, ‘There is nothing but our worldly life. We die and we live.’” That is, there is nothing but this abode. Some people die and others live, and there is no Resurrection or resurrection. This is what the polytheists of the Arabs who deny the Resurrection say, and it is what the divine philosophers among them say, and they deny the beginning and the return. It is what the materialist philosophers of the Deity say, who deny the Creator, and who believe that every thirty-six thousand years everything returns to what it was. They claimed that this has been repeated countless times, so they were stubborn about reason and denied what was transmitted. For this reason they said, And nothing destroys us except time. God Almighty said: “And they have no knowledge of that. They only conjecture.” That is, they imagine and fantasize. As for the hadith that the two authors of the Sahih, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i, narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God said: God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, says: The son of Adam offends Me by cursing time, while I am time. In My hand is the command; I alternate its night and day.” In another narration: Do not curse time, for God is time. Ibn Jarir included it in a very strange context, saying: Abu Kurayb told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The people of ignorance used to say: It is only the night and the day that destroy us, that it is He who destroys us; He causes us to die and brings us to life. So God, the Almighty, said in His Book: ‘And they say: There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time.’ And they curse time. So God, the Almighty, said: The son of Adam offends Me by cursing time, while I am time. In My hand is the command; I alternate the night and the day.” Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it similarly, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Mansur, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah. Then he narrated on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty said: ‘The son of Adam curses time, but I am time. In My hand are the night and the day.’” And the two authors of the Sahih and Al-Nasa’i included it on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘God the Most High says, “I borrowed from My servant but he did not give Me, and My servant cursed Me.” He says, Woe to him! And I am time.” Al-Shafi’i, Abu Ubaidah, and other imams said in their interpretation of the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Do not curse time, for God is time. When the Arabs in their pre-Islamic period were afflicted with hardship, calamity, or misfortune, they would say, Oh, what a disaster time is! They would attribute those actions to time and curse it, but the one who did them was God the Most High. It was as if they were cursing God, the Almighty, because He is the one who did that in reality. For this reason, cursing time in this regard was forbidden, because God the Most High is the time they mean and to which they attribute those actions. This is the best that has been said in its interpretation, and it is what is intended, and God knows best. Ibn Hazm and those who followed his example among the Zahiris erred in counting time as one of the Most Beautiful Names, taking this hadith as evidence. God the Almighty says: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, meaning when the truth is explained to them and God the Almighty is able to restore bodies after they have perished and been scattered, Their only argument is that they say, ‘Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful,’ meaning, bring them back to life if what you say is true. God the Almighty says: Say, ‘God gives you life and then causes you to die,’ meaning, as you see, He brings you out of nonexistence into existence. How can you disbelieve in God while you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die and then bring you back to life? That is, He who was able to begin is able to repeat it, by a fortiori and more appropriate way. And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. “Then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.” That is, He will only assemble you for the Day of Resurrection. He will not bring you back in this world until you say, Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful. “The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly.” For what day have you postponed? For the Day of Separation. “And We do not delay it except for a specified term.” And He said here, Then He will assemble you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. That is, there is no doubt about it. But most of the people do not know. That is, for this reason they deny the Resurrection and rule out the resurrection of bodies. God Almighty said, Indeed, they see it as far off, but We see it as near. That is, they see its occurrence as far off, while the believers see it as easy and near.

Ibn Jarir included it in a very strange context, saying: Abu Kurayb told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The people of ignorance used to say: It is only the night and the day that destroy us, that it is He who destroys us; He causes us to die and brings us to life. God the Almighty says: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, meaning when the truth is explained to them and God the Almighty is able to restore bodies after they have perished and been scattered, Their only argument is that they say, ‘Bring our fathers, if you should be truthful,’ meaning, bring them back to life if what you say is true. 45:27: God Almighty tells us that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and the Ruler of them in this world and the hereafter. That is why He, the Almighty, said: And on the Day the Hour comes meaning the Day of Resurrection the falsifiers will lose - they are the disbelievers in God who deny what He sent down to His Messengers of clear signs and evident proofs. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sufyan al-Thawri came to Madinah and heard al-Ma'afiri saying something that would make people laugh. He said to him: O Sheikh, don't you know that God has a day on which the falsifiers will lose? He said: This reputation continued to grow in al-Ma'afiri until he joined God. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned this, then God the Almighty said: And you will see every nation kneeling, meaning on its knees from the severity and greatness. It is said that when Hell is brought, it will sigh and no one will remain except kneeling, even Abraham, peace be upon him, who will say: Myself, myself, myself! I ask You today for nothing but myself. Even Jesus, peace be upon him, will say: "I ask You for nothing but myself. I ask You for Mary who gave birth to me!" Mujahid, Ka'b al-Ahbar, and al-Hasan al-Basri said: Every nation kneeling, meaning on its knees. Ikrimah said: Kneeling distinctly on its side, not on its knees, but the former is more appropriate. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri narrated to us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Babaah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is as if I see you kneeling in a heap before Hellfire. Ismail ibn Abi Rafi’ al-Madani said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of the trumpet: “Then the people will be distinguished and the nations will kneel, and it is about this that God, the Most High, says: ‘And you will see every nation kneeling, every nation called to its book.’” This combines the two opinions and there is no contradiction, and God knows best. That is why He, the Almighty, said: This Day you will be recompensed for what you used to do, meaning you will be recompensed for your deeds, both good and bad, as He, the Almighty, said: “On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forth and what he left behind. Rather, man will be a witness against himself, even if he were to put forth his excuses.” That is why He, the Almighty, said: This is Our Book that speaks against you with truth, meaning it will bring to mind all your deeds, neither addition nor subtraction, as He, the Almighty, said: “And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, ‘Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has enumerated it?’ And they will find what they did present. Then He recited: Indeed, We were recording what you used to do.
